19304-secret-history-revealed-by-lady-pe.title: Secret History Revealed By Lady Peggy O Malley
19304-secret-history-revealed-by-lady-pe.creator: Clarence Rowe
19304-secret-history-revealed-by-lady-pe.description: A book by Clarence Rowe. One month before I met the white dress, Diana and Father and I had come from home--that's Ballyconal--to see what good we could do with a season in London; good for Diana, I mean, and I put her before Father because he does so himself. Every one else he puts far, far behind, like the beasts following Noah into the Ark.

arxiv-1601-02980.title: The sensitivity of past and near-future lunar radio experiments to ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and neutrinos Journal: Astroparticle Physics
arxiv-1601-02980.creator: J.D. Bray
arxiv-1601-02980.description: Abstract Various experiments have been conducted to search for the radio emission from ultra-high-energy particles interacting in the lunar regolith. Although they have not yielded any detections, they have been successful in establishing upper limits on the flux of these particles.

arxiv-2102-02062.title: Accurate prediction of machining feedrate and cycle time considering interpolator dynamics Journal: International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
arxiv-2102-02062.creator: Rob Ward, Burak Sencer, Bryn Jones, Erdem Ozturk
arxiv-2102-02062.description: Abstract This paper presents an accurate machining feedrate prediction technique by modeling the trajectory generation behaviour of modern CNC machine tools. Typically, CAM systems simulate machines’ motion based on the commanded feedrate and the path geometry. Such approach does not consider the feed planning and interpolation strategy of the machine’s numerical control (NC) system.

arxiv-2109-09367.title: Extending bootstrap AMG for clustering of attributed graphs
arxiv-2109-09367.creator: Pasqua D’Ambra, Panayot S. Vassilevski, Luisa Cutillo
arxiv-2109-09367.description: Abstract . In this paper we propose a new approach to detect clusters in undirected graphs with attributed vertices. We incorporate structural and attribute similarities between the vertices in an augmented graph by creating additional vertices and edges as proposed in [ 1 , 2 ] .

arxiv-2302-10038.title: The G G -index, G G -coindex and G G -weight of a real moment-angle complex
arxiv-2302-10038.creator: Akatsuki Kizu
arxiv-2302-10038.description: Abstract . A real moment-angle complex is a CW complex defined by the combinatoric information of a simplicial complex, and has a standard action of 2 2 -torus. For each subtorus G G of 2 2 -torus, we describe invariants corcerning this action, the G G -index, G G -coindex and G G -weight, combinatorially. 1.

arxiv-2312-11522.title: Assessing SATNet’s Ability to Solve the Symbol Grounding Problem
arxiv-2312-11522.creator: Oscar Chang, Lampros Flokas, Hod Lipson, Michael Spranger
arxiv-2312-11522.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Oscar Chang, Lampros Flokas, Hod Lipson, Michael Spranger. SATNet is an award-winning MAXSAT solver that can be used to infer logical rules and integrated as a differentiable layer in a deep neural network [ 1 ] . It had been shown to solve Sudoku puzzles visually from examples of puzzle digit images, and was heralded as an impressive achievement towards the longstanding AI goal of combining pattern recognition with logical reasoning.

arxiv-2401-16281.title: Semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering at NNLO in QCD Preprint: ZU-TH 07/24
arxiv-2401-16281.creator: Leonardo Bonino, Thomas Gehrmann, Giovanni Stagnitto
arxiv-2401-16281.description: Abstract Semi-inclusive hadron production processes in deep-inelastic lepton-nucleon scattering are important probes of the quark flavour structure of the nucleon and of the fragmentation dynamics of quarks into hadrons. We compute the full next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) QCD corrections to the coefficient functions for semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS) in analytical form.

arxiv-2403-17604.title: Massless fermions in black string spacetime
arxiv-2403-17604.creator: R. Darlla, Ö. Yeşiltaş, J. Furtado
arxiv-2403-17604.description: Abstract In this paper we investigate the behaviour of massless fermions in the black string spacetime by computing the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the Weyl equations. These solutions allowed us to study the behaviour of such massless fermions in terms of the cosmological constant, the black string’s mass and the radial distance of the particle from the black string.

arxiv-2411-09549.title: Quantum computing inspired paintings: reinterpreting classical masterpieces
arxiv-2411-09549.creator: Arianna Crippa, Yahui Chai, Omar Costa Hamido, Paulo Itaborai, Karl Jansen, QC-PAINT
arxiv-2411-09549.description: Abstract We aim to apply a quantum computing technique to compose artworks. The main idea is to revisit three paintings of different styles and historical periods: “ Narciso ”, painted circa 1597–1599 by Michelangelo Merisi (Caravaggio), “ Les fils de l’homme ”, painted in 1964 by René Magritte and “ 192 Farben ”, painted in 1966 by Gerard Richter.

arxiv-2504-14496.title: Functional Abstraction of Knowledge Recall in Large Language Models
arxiv-2504-14496.creator: Zijian Wang, Chang Xu
arxiv-2504-14496.description: Abstract Pre-trained transformer large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong knowledge recall capabilities. This paper investigates the knowledge recall mechanism in LLMs by abstracting it into a functional structure. We propose that during knowledge recall, the model’s hidden activation space implicitly entails a function execution process where specific activation vectors align with functional components (Input argument, Function body, and Return values).

arxiv-2509-17562.title: Visual Instruction Pretraining for Domain-Specific Foundation Models
arxiv-2509-17562.creator: Yuxuan Li, Yicheng Zhang, Wenhao Tang, Yimian Dai Ming-Ming Cheng Xiang Li Jian Yang
arxiv-2509-17562.description: Abstract Modern computer vision is converging on a closed loop in which perception, reasoning and generation mutually reinforce each other. However, this loop remains incomplete: the top-down influence of high-level reasoning on the foundational learning of low-level perceptual features is not yet underexplored. This paper addresses this gap by proposing a new paradigm for pretraining foundation models in downstream domains.

pmc-10586174.title: Annealing Effect on Mechanical and Tribological Behaviors of Nanoscale Mechanics of Zr60Cu25Al5Ag5Ni5 Thin-Layer Metallic Glasses for Engineering Materials Applications
pmc-10586174.creator: Adem Ali Muhabie, Wubshet Mekonnen Girma
pmc-10586174.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). A new and unique alloy formulation design strategy has been developed in order to fabricate thin-layered metallic glasses (TLMGs) with superior fracture resistance and low coefficient of friction (COF) during the nanoscratching test. Due to the outstanding properties, TFMG could be applied for different uses, such as for surface coating, biomedical, bioimprinting, electronic devices, spacecraft, and railway, all of which need surface fracture resistance.

pmc-10655535.title: Hemoglobin Levels Improve Fracture Risk Prediction in Addition to FRAX Clinical Risk Factors and Bone Mineral Density
pmc-10655535.creator: Raju Jaiswal, Helena Johansson, Kristian F Axelsson, Per Magnusson, Nicholas C Harvey, Liesbeth Vandenput, Eugene McCloskey, John A Kanis, Henrik Litsne, Lisa Johansson, Mattias Lorentzon
pmc-10655535.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). ContextAnemia and decreasing levels of hemoglobin (Hb) have previously been linked to increased fracture risk, but the added value to FRAX, the most utilized fracture prediction tool worldwide, is unknown.ObjectiveTo investigate the association between anemia, Hb levels, bone microstructure, and risk of incident fracture and to evaluate whether Hb levels improve fracture risk prediction in addition to FRAX clinical risk factors (CRFs).MethodsA total of 2778 community-dwelling women, aged 75-80 years, and part of a prospective population-based cohort study in Sweden were included.

pmc-10743290.description: The surge in the implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) in recent years has permeated many aspects of our life, and health care is no exception. Whereas this technology can offer clear benefits, some of the problems associated with its use have also been recognised and brought into question, for example, its environmental impact.

pmc-12514478.title: Clinical utility of runs of homozygosity in the identification of genetic causes in individuals with rare diseases
pmc-12514478.creator: Theru A Sivakumaran, Bilal Azab, Emily Hershman, Ananditha Sivakumaran, Neil R Friedman, Dannah Raz, Derek Neilson, Theresa A Grebe
pmc-12514478.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). PurposeTo evaluate the clinical utility of runs of homozygosity (ROH) in identifying the genetic causes of rare diseases in our patient population.MethodsAll unrelated patients (N = 2787), presenting with neurodevelopmental disorders and/or congenital anomalies, who underwent chromosomal microarray testing in our laboratory between July 2019 and December 2023, and publicly available single-nucleotide polymorphism microarray data from 3488 unrelated individuals in the general population were included in this study.

pmc-12643453.title: Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension in Pregnancy with Aggravated Comorbidity: A Case Report and Review of Diagnostic and Management Challenges
pmc-12643453.creator: Taruna Agrawal, Jhia Jiat Teh, Konstantinos S. Kechagias, Zak Jefferson-Pillai, Kanwaljeet Kaur Sandhu, Sarah-Jane Lam
pmc-12643453.description: Background and Clinical Significance: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) is a rare cause of headache characterised by cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage, with an estimated incidence of 3.7 to 5 cases per 100,000 per year, peaking around the age of 40 years. Its diagnosis and management are particularly challenging in pregnancy due to overlapping symptoms and limited diagnostic options.

pmc-12716759.title: Dual niche modeling with GEE and SHAP for predicting habitat shifts of Haloxylon ammodendron and Cistanche deserticola under climate change
pmc-12716759.creator: Jing-Xia Guo, Yan Wu, Teng-Da Zhang, Feng-Long Lv, Yi-Fan Gong
pmc-12716759.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Haloxylon ammodendron, a keystone woody species, and its parasitic plant, Cistanche deserticola, play critical roles in sustaining arid ecosystems and supporting regional economies. However, their distribution is increasingly threatened by global climate change. Here, we propose a dual niche modeling framework that integrates climate and soil suitability layers using a multi-model ensemble approach combined with interpretable machine-learning techniques, specifically SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Using CMIP6 scenarios (SSP126, SSP245, and SSP585), we predicted the current and future potential habitats for both species.

uslaw-usc-t17-s1302.title: 17 U.S.C. § 1302 — Designs not subject to protection
uslaw-usc-t17-s1302.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t17-s1302.description: United States Code, Title 17 (Copyrights); Chapter 13 (Protection Of Original Designs). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Protection under this chapter shall not be available for a design that is— (1) not original; (2) staple or commonplace, such as a standard geometric figure, a familiar symbol, an emblem, or a motif, or another shape, pattern, or configuration which has become standard, common.
